nary_nodes.label: War on Iran
evidence: the United States and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February

nary_nodes.label: Oil price swings
evidence: Oil prices have swung from levels not seen since the onset of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to close to where they were before the conflict more than four months ago.

nary_nodes.label: Disruption of trade routes
evidence: Energy suppliers have scrambled to find alternative trade routes amid Iran’s stranglehold over the Strait of Hormuz

nary_nodes.label: Emergency measures by governments
evidence: governments have rolled emergency measures to spare citizens from the worst of the pain inflicted by surging fuel costs.

nary_nodes.label: US-Iran negotiations
evidence: ongoing US-Iran negotiations to reach a lasting peace

nary_nodes.label: Pipeline expansion efforts
evidence: energy suppliers have sought to ramp up exports on land via Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the United Arab Emirates’ Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline, and the Iraq-Turkiye Crude Oil Pipeline

nary_nodes.label: Attacks on commercial vessels
evidence: Attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz are widely expected to have a chilling effect on shipping lines

nary_nodes.label: Drop in maritime traffic
evidence: maritime traffic dropped sharply again over the weekend after attacks on two commercial ships

nary_nodes.label: Acceleration of renewable energy shift
evidence: an acceleration in countries’ efforts to shift from fossil fuels to renewables

nary_nodes.label: Investment decisions brought forward
evidence: The conflict may ultimately bring forward investment decisions that were already in motion

nary_nodes.label: Oil price levels
evidence: Oil prices have swung from levels not seen since the onset of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to close to where they were before the conflict more than four months ago.

nary_nodes.label: Strait transit volume
evidence: approximately 20 million barrels of oil that moved through the strait each day before the war

nary_nodes.label: Pipeline combined capacity
evidence: the pipelines’ combined capacity falls well short of the approximately 20 million barrels of oil that moved through the strait each day before the war

nary_nodes.label: Renewable energy capacity record
evidence: Global renewable energy capacity hit a record high in 2025, with non-fossil fuel projects accounting for approximately 86 percent of added power capacity that year

nary_nodes.label: China's renewable component exports
evidence: producing more than 80 percent of the world’s wind turbines, solar panels and energy storage batteries

nary_nodes.label: Oil market never the same
evidence: “The oil market will never be the same, following this conflict,” Adi Imsirovic

nary_nodes.label: New pipelines and security arrangements
evidence: “New pipelines will urgently be built. New security arrangements will be put into place, and the buyers of oil from the region will look elsewhere for diversification,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Long-term concern over transits
evidence: Dan Marks ... said he expects there to be “long-term” concern over transits in the strait.

nary_nodes.label: Sustained push to reduce reliance
evidence: June Goh ... said she anticipates a sustained push by energy producers and consumers alike to reduce their reliance on the strait.

nary_nodes.label: Conflict supercharging renewables boom
evidence: Simon Stiell ... told a meeting ... that the conflict was already “supercharging the global renewables boom”.

nary_nodes.label: End of oil monopoly in road transport
evidence: “And this will finish the important monopoly of oil in road transportation,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Economic case for renewables strengthens
evidence: the medium to long-term economic case for renewables will strengthen as geopolitical risk inflates “the true cost” of fossil fuel dependence, said Mohamed Elheddad

nary_nodes.label: China benefits from energy shift
evidence: “China will benefit, given its dominance in providing renewable energy infrastructure products,” Obstfeld told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: US and Qatar consolidate positions
evidence: Other countries such as the US and Qatar may also be able to consolidate their positions as leading energy suppliers in the aftermath of the war, said Elheddad
